summary: Martin Lookout, a 30-foot pole tower near the Martin rail stop, built around 1932 and gone; footings found in 2015.

facts.status_note: The lookout is gone; footings were found in 2015.

visit.trail_note: Under one mile to the tunnel and about 1/4 mile to the lookout site, per Willhite. The railroad would prefer visitors not be there.

events.note: Around 1932 per the register, which gives the 1930s; a photo captioned as under construction is dated 1932.
Morris Jenkins listed as known lookout personnel.
Willhite found the footings just north of the power lines.

evidence.supports: Tower built around 1932, 30 foot pole tower
evidence.quote: Around 1932 a 30 foot pole tower was constructed on the site.
Martin Lookout under construction 1932 - courtesy of Eric Willhite collection

evidence.supports: Administered by the U.S. Forest Service
Site lies in the Wenatchee National Forest
Around 1932, 30 foot pole tower, gone, personnel 1933 Morris Jenkins
evidence.quote: 1932+-: 30' pole tower. Gone. Known lookout personnel: 1933: Morris Jenkins.

evidence.supports: Martin was a Northern Pacific stop at the east portal of the tunnel
evidence.quote: Martin was a stop on the Northern Pacific rail line at the east portal of the Stampede Pass Tunnel.

evidence.supports: Town built during tunnel construction, 1886 to 1888
evidence.quote: The town of Martin was built up during construction of the tunnel (between 1886 and 1888)

evidence.supports: Only a little of the town remains
evidence.quote: Not much of the town is left

evidence.supports: Visitors get a view of the East Portal from the tracks
evidence.quote: get a view of the East Portal of the tunnel

evidence.supports: Two visits needed to find the exact spot
evidence.quote: Finding the exact location of the Martin Lookout took two visits.

evidence.supports: Footings found in 2015 just north of the power lines
evidence.quote: In 2015 I went back and found the footings just feet north the powerlines.

evidence.supports: Walk distances to tunnel and lookout
evidence.quote: Easy walk under one mile to tunnel, 1/4 mile to lookout

evidence.supports: Railroad would prefer visitors not be there; visitors walk the tracks
evidence.quote: Although the railroad would prefer you not there, it is very common for visitors to be walking along the tracks taking a look at the tunnel.
the ski trail goes between the footings.

evidence.supports: Photo captioned as decaying wood and bolts

corrections.why: The register's Built field says 1930's and its description says around 1932; the 1932 construction photo agrees with 1932, not 1930.
The register's detail page lists N 47.266311, W 121.311327. The current point is about 1.4 km north-northwest of that.

sources.title: Martin Lookout and the Stampede Tunnel

notes_for_editor: Build date is only approximate (1930s, around 1932). The Willhite Access section gives directions only (park, then walk past a gate up to the tracks) and states no access rule, so no source says whether the site is open to the public. The Meany Lodge history page (history.meanylodge.org/Building/Martin-Lookout/) appeared in search but was not read. No fire history found in these sources. The brief's coordinates sit about 1.4 km from the register's listed point; that correction is in corrections. This file has no coordinate field, so that correction is still pending for the editor.
